# Agent 4: Features B — Deals, Curated Sections, Detail Page & Comparison

## Your Role
Build the deal-focused sections, laptop detail page, and side-by-side comparison feature. These complete the user journey from browsing to evaluating to buying.

## Before You Start
You are building a production app for real users — not a demo, not a prototype. Every component should be production-ready.

Read every file in `.gemini/antigravity/brain/` — especially spec.md, copy.md, and api-contract.md.
Read `.antigravity/rules.md` for code quality and security rules.

## Important Context
- This is a laptop price comparison site — your features are the "payoff" of the browsing experience
- Detail page is where users decide to buy (affiliate links to retailers)
- Comparison feature is a key differentiator vs competitors
- Deal ratings: Great Price (green, ≥15% below median), Fair Price (amber, within 15%), Above Average (red, >15% above)
- No user accounts/auth in v1

## Build Order

### Feature 1: Laptop Detail Page (P0)
1. Create `src/app/(features)/laptop/[slug]/page.tsx` — Fetches from `/api/laptops/[slug]`. Server component for SEO. Include `loading.tsx` and `error.tsx`.
2. Create `src/components/features/detail/spec-table.tsx` — Full specs in a structured table. All fields from the Laptop model. Uses JetBrains Mono for technical values.
3. Create `src/components/features/detail/retailer-prices.tsx` — List of ALL retailer prices as clickable rows: "Buy at [Retailer] — $[price]". Each row shows: retailer name, price (JetBrains Mono), original price (strikethrough if discounted), discount %, stock status, "Price checked X minutes ago" freshness indicator. Stale prices (>2 hours) get warning badge "Price may be outdated". Out-of-stock shows "Currently unavailable". Buy links open in new tab (affiliate links).
4. Create `src/components/features/detail/review-summary.tsx` — Review score display (if available) with review count.
5. Create `src/components/features/detail/detail-hero.tsx` — Large product image with fallback + deal rating badge + key specs summary.

### Feature 2: Top Deals Section (P1)
6. Create `src/app/(features)/deals/page.tsx` — Fetches from `/api/deals`. Laptop cards sorted by discount percentage. Include loading/error states.
7. Create `src/components/features/deals/deal-card.tsx` — Enhanced laptop card that prominently features the discount percentage and price drop.

### Feature 3: Budget Picks Section (P1)
8. Create `src/app/(features)/budget-picks/page.tsx` — Fetches from `/api/budget-picks`. Optional max price filter. Include loading/error states.

### Feature 4: Best Rated Section (P1)
9. Create `src/app/(features)/best-rated/page.tsx` — Fetches from `/api/best-rated`. Shows review scores prominently. Include loading/error states.

### Feature 5: Side-by-Side Comparison (P1)
10. Create `src/hooks/use-comparison.ts` — Manages comparison state. Stores selected laptop slugs in URL params (e.g., `?compare=slug1,slug2,slug3`). Max 3 laptops. Provides: `addToCompare(slug)`, `removeFromCompare(slug)`, `clearComparison()`, `comparedSlugs`, `isAtLimit`, `isComparing(slug)`.
11. Create `src/components/features/comparison/compare-checkbox.tsx` — Checkbox component for laptop cards. Disabled when limit (3) reached and this laptop isn't already selected. Integrates with use-comparison hook.
12. Create `src/components/features/comparison/comparison-tray-content.tsx` — Content for the sticky bottom tray (Foundation agent builds the tray shell). Shows "Compare (X of 3)", small thumbnails of selected laptops, "Compare Now" button (enabled ≥2), "Clear all" link.
13. Create `src/app/(features)/compare/page.tsx` — Full comparison page. Fetches detail data for each compared laptop. Side-by-side table with specs as rows and laptops as columns. Price comparison rows per retailer. Visual highlights for "best" value in each spec row (e.g., lowest price, most RAM, best battery).

### Testing
14. Write E2E tests:
    - Detail page: navigate to a laptop, verify specs table, verify retailer prices, verify buy links
    - Comparison: select 2 laptops, click Compare Now, verify comparison table
    - Deals page: verify discount sorting
15. Run `npm test`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Detail page shows full specs, all retailer prices, review score
- [ ] Every retailer row has clickable affiliate buy link (opens new tab)
- [ ] "Price checked X minutes ago" freshness indicator works
- [ ] Stale price warning badge shows for >2 hour old prices
- [ ] Out-of-stock retailers show "Currently unavailable"
- [ ] Top Deals page shows laptops sorted by discount %
- [ ] Budget Picks page shows best value laptops with optional price cap
- [ ] Best Rated page shows highest review scores
- [ ] Compare checkbox works on laptop cards (adds/removes from comparison)
- [ ] Comparison tray shows count, thumbnails, and Compare Now button
- [ ] Comparison page renders side-by-side spec table for 2-3 laptops
- [ ] Comparison state persists in URL params across navigation
- [ ] Max 3 laptops enforced — additional checkboxes disabled at limit
- [ ] All pages have loading.tsx (skeleton) and error.tsx
- [ ] All copy from copy.md — no placeholder text
- [ ] E2E tests pass for detail, comparison, and deals flows

## Coordination
You run in parallel with Foundation (layout/shared), API (backend), and Agent 3 (browsing/filters).

Since they're building at the same time:
- Use CSS variables from design-tokens.json directly
- Use endpoint paths from api-contract.md directly (e.g., `fetch('/api/laptops/${slug}')`, `fetch('/api/deals')`)
- Import shared components by expected paths (e.g., `import { LaptopCard } from '@/components/shared/laptop-card'`, `import { DealBadge } from '@/components/shared/deal-badge'`)
- The comparison tray shell is built by Foundation agent — you build the CONTENT that goes inside it
- The compare checkbox integrates into laptop cards — coordinate by exporting a `CompareCheckbox` component that the card can render
- If a shared component isn't available yet, build a local placeholder and note it for later refactoring
